purpose: Fresh development transfer questions, withheld from construction. Not a blinded benchmark.

cases.question: Our async HTTP service spends most request time in a pure-Python validation loop. We plan to replace 'validate(payload)' with an async def that performs the same loop, with no awaits. Will that improve parallelism or responsiveness? Suggest a measured design without inventing a performance target.
required: async declaration does not offload CPU work
measure and choose process or other execution with overhead considered

cases.question: Does 'Python 3.14 uses forkserver on POSIX' mean our macOS laptop and Linux workers have the same multiprocessing default? Explain how a library should handle caller-selected contexts and what fork deprecation actually means.
required: fork not universally removed or deprecated; warning for multithreaded fork

cases.question: A filtered tar extraction refused a member after writing several earlier members. Can we continue using that directory as a successfully validated upload, or just retry with fully_trusted? Explain the recovery and isolation design.
required: fresh isolated destination and controlled cleanup

cases.question: Our editable install passes tests. We want to certify the wheel by running pytest from the repository root after installing it into the same environment. What can still be masked, and what would a credible artifact check do?
required: editable and checkout can mask artifact omissions
fresh environment and outside-checkout installed-wheel test
inspect package data and imports without assuming one build backend
no guarantee from pytest mode alone

cases.question: A formatting migration would change a public function name and break callers, solely to satisfy a style checker. What should a Python engineering expert recommend and why?
required: compatibility takes priority over cosmetic style
do not invent benchmark or productivity thresholds
